title: Lower trace cardinality and replace JSON logger with pooled serializer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several backend services are emitting extremely high-cardinality span attributes (user_id, session_token, request_digest) and verbose JSON logs per request. At 5k+ RPS this manifests as: explosion of distinct metric and span labels, increased Prometheus exporter cardinality, heavy CPU and GC due to JSON marshalling, and slow query/ingest on our trace backend.

Goal: Reduce telemetry cardinality and per-request allocation without losing actionable signal. Deliver a low-risk rollout that preserves security/PII constraints, provides an audit trail for hashed identifiers, and gives forward-compatible knobs for tuning sampling and exporter batching.

Scope: this ticket covers the service instrumentation shim and logger layer in the Go and Node service templates, OpenTelemetry SDK config and exporter batching defaults, and a lightweight adaptive sampling shim that lives in the tracer initialization path. It also includes a drop-in pooled log serializer and a migration guide for libraries and service owners.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate span cardinality per service reduced by >=30% for top 10 high-volume endpoints in canary traffic
End-to-end P99 CPU for canary services reduced by >=20% (measured under production-like load)
JSON allocations per-request reduced by >=60% as measured by runtime/pprof heap profiles
No raw user identifiers emitted in span attributes or logs; hashed mapping stored in an internal reversible mapping service for debugging (access-controlled)
Adaptive sampling shim can be toggled via feature flag and adjusts sampling rate based on error rate and latency spikes
Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK client to target version and exporter batching knobs documented in PRD
Canary run completed with rollback plan and no customer-facing incidents
plan: Design attribute normalization table: enumerate attributes considered high-cardinality and define bucketization/hash policy
Implement attribute normalization middleware in Go/Node instrumentation libraries; add opt-out hooks for legacy services
Introduce adaptive sampling shim: initial algorithm uses sliding window error and latency thresholds to temporarily increase sampling; expose metrics for sampled vs unsampled traces
Replace current JSON logger with pooled serializer using preallocated buffers and zero-copy writer API; add fallback to existing logger via env var
Adjust OTLP exporter batching config (max_export_batch_size, scheduled_delay_millis) and upgrade client SDK to the chosen stable version
Add unit and integration tests validating no PII leakage and correct hash mappings; add e2e perf harness (k6) to measure allocations and CPU
Run a two-stage canary: internal traffic -> 5% production traffic -> 25% production traffic, monitor key signals and iterate
Documentation: migration guide, runbook, and dashboard updates; announce in #infra-observability
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive normalization could remove useful debug information. Mitigation: keep reversible hashed mapping service with strict RBAC and audit logs; add 'debug-keep' annotation for PRs during troubleshooting

Risk: Serializer change introduces subtle formatting differences breaking downstream parsers. Mitigation: run log-compatibility tests with current parsers (ELK/Fluentd) and retain compatibility mode behind flag
Risk: Adaptive sampling hides rare but important errors. Mitigation: sampling shim increases sample rate on error spikes and creates a small persistent reservoir of traces per minute
Risk: SDK upgrade surface regressions. Mitigation: upgrade in a feature branch, run CI integration suite, and test canary with long-tail load
